name: Porsche 959 Sport
description:
The Porsche 959 Sport represents the ultimate expression of Porsche's groundbreaking Group B homologation supercar—a lightweight, track-focused variant that strips away luxury in favor of pure performance. While the standard 959 balanced cutting-edge technology with grand touring comfort, the Sport version embodied Porsche's racing philosophy: reduce weight, maximize performance, and give serious drivers the machine they truly wanted.

Developed in the early 1980s as Porsche's answer to Group B domination, the 959 required 200 production units for homologation. The Sport variant took this already revolutionary platform and shed approximately 100 kg by eliminating air conditioning, power windows, rear seats, and luxury sound insulation. What remained was 1,375 kg of precisely engineered performance machinery, making this the lightest and most focused 959 variant available.

At the heart of the 959 Sport lies Porsche's twin-turbocharged 2.85-liter flat-six producing 450 horsepower and 501 Nm of torque. The innovative sequential twin-turbo system eliminated traditional turbo lag by using a small turbo for low-end response and a larger one for high-rpm power—technology that was years ahead of its time. In the Sport variant, this power feels even more immediate thanks to the reduced mass and track-oriented suspension tuning.

The sophisticated PSK (Porsche-Steuer Kupplung) all-wheel-drive system features driver-selectable torque distribution across four programs, from dry tarmac to competition settings. Combined with adjustable ride height suspension, tire pressure monitoring, and advanced aerodynamics, the 959 Sport delivered capabilities that seemed almost alien in the 1980s. The result: 0-100 km/h in just 3.7 seconds and a top speed exceeding 339 km/h—making it one of the fastest production cars in the world when introduced.

Though Group B's cancellation prevented the 959 from achieving its intended racing glory, the Sport variant became the purist's choice—the 959 for those who prioritized performance over comfort. Its technological innovations—all-wheel drive, advanced engine management, sophisticated aerodynamics—eventually influenced future 911 generations. Today, the 959 Sport stands as the most driver-focused example of one of automotive history's most significant supercars.
